brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clear semantic color coding (green=healthy, amber=stressed) ties state to hue with immediate legibility
Strong percentage typography hierarchy makes the vital number the unmistakable focal point of each card
Emoji-in-rounded-tile iconography adds personality consistent with the 'organism' metaphor brief
dominant_weaknesses: The 'breathing/pulsing' organism metaphor is invisible in a static frame — no waveform, sparkline, or rhythm visualization carries the concept
Massive vertical dead space between the status line and the percentage leaves cards feeling hollow and uncomposed
Bottom stat chips (16 Cores, 32GB, 98.2°F) appear only on the right card, breaking symmetry and visual parallelism
fix_priorities: Add a literal breathing/pulsing waveform or sine line whose amplitude and frequency encode load — this IS the brief
Rebalance vertical rhythm: pull the percentage up, anchor metadata chips to both cards consistently
Differentiate stressed state more viscerally — warmer glow, faster cadence, subtle red bleed at >75%
Tighten typographic scale: status sublabels are too quiet relative to the giant percentage
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leans on color and big numerals, but behavioral feedback (the actual organism rhythm) is missing, leaving reflective meaning thin.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the color/label states gesture at organism health, but without motion or rhythmic visualization the 'breathes vs pulses' concept never actually manifests.
